what_happened: Dispatch's grep pattern (*implementation-agent.md) does not match the 3 hard-mode implementation agents (cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md, lean-implementation-hard-agent.md, books-implementation-hard-agent.md), which also have zero mentions of modified_files -- the same bug, outside the literally-named scope. Flagged in the research report (Finding 1 scope note, Recommendation 7) for the plan to decide whether to fold in.

Research report identified an existing in-repo propagation mechanism (canonical fragment + lint-agent-contracts.sh Check C/G/H pattern) plus the exact next free check letter, so plan construction was mechanical rather than exploratory.

The dispatch's SCOPE glob (*implementation-agent.md) structurally cannot match *-implementation-hard-agent.md, so three hard-mode agents with the identical defect were never counted; plan deliberately widens scope from 10 to 13 agents and isolates the widening in its own phase.

The track-on-write canonical line was inserted word-wrapped across 3-4 physical lines in all 13 Phase 2-4 agent files for readability. Phase 2-4's own grep -cF verification used a truncated anchor substring that only spanned the first wrapped line, so it reported 1 match and passed even though the full canonical line never appeared as a single physical line. This was only caught when Check L's own runtime grep -F extraction of the full line from the fragment failed to match any of the 13 files in Phase 5. Fixed by collapsing the track-on-write line to a single physical line in all 13 files before finishing Check L.
